steps.note: Trigger function that keeps the new bigint column equal to customer_id on every insert/update.
steps.sql: CREATE OR REPLACE FUNCTION orders_customer_id_sync() RETURNS trigger LANGUAGE plpgsql AS $$ BEGIN NEW.customer_id_new := NEW.customer_id; RETURN NEW; END $$;

steps.note: In one short transaction: add nullable customer_id_new bigint (metadata only, no rewrite), a NOT VALID not-null check, and the sync trigger. The table lock is taken with a 300ms lock_timeout and retried, so app queries never queue behind it for long.
steps.sql: DO $$ DECLARE tries int := 0; BEGIN LOOP BEGIN PERFORM set_config('lock_timeout', '300ms', true); LOCK TABLE orders IN ACCESS EXCLUSIVE MODE; ALTER TABLE orders ADD COLUMN customer_id_new bigint; ALTER TABLE orders ADD CONSTRAINT orders_customer_id_new_check CHECK (customer_id_new IS NOT NULL) NOT VALID; CREATE TRIGGER orders_customer_id_sync BEFORE INSERT OR UPDATE ON orders FOR EACH ROW EXECUTE FUNCTION orders_customer_id_sync(); EXIT; EXCEPTION WHEN lock_not_available THEN tries := tries + 1; IF tries >= 100 THEN RAISE; END IF; PERFORM pg_sleep(0.2); END; END LOOP; END $$;

steps.note: Backfill ids 1..1,000,000 in 250k-row batches, each its own transaction (the app only inserts new rows, so no row-lock conflicts).

steps.note: Backfill rows above 10,000,000 that the app inserted before the trigger existed (rows inserted after it already have the value).
steps.sql: SET statement_timeout = 0; UPDATE orders SET customer_id_new = customer_id WHERE id > 10000000 AND customer_id_new IS DISTINCT FROM customer_id;

steps.note: Verify every row: customer_id_new must equal customer_id, otherwise the plan stops here. Plain read, takes no blocking lock.
steps.sql: SET statement_timeout = 0; DO $$ DECLARE n bigint; BEGIN SELECT count(*) INTO n FROM orders WHERE customer_id_new IS DISTINCT FROM customer_id; IF n > 0 THEN RAISE EXCEPTION '% rows have customer_id_new <> customer_id', n; END IF; END $$;

steps.note: Validate the not-null check. VALIDATE takes only SHARE UPDATE EXCLUSIVE, so reads and inserts keep running; once valid, SET NOT NULL can skip its table scan.
steps.sql: SET statement_timeout = 0; ALTER TABLE orders VALIDATE CONSTRAINT orders_customer_id_new_check;

steps.note: Atomic swap, metadata only, same short-lock-with-retry pattern: SET NOT NULL (proven by the valid check, no scan), drop the check and the trigger, drop the old integer column, rename customer_id_new to customer_id. The app refers to columns by name, so it needs no redeploy.
steps.sql: DO $$ DECLARE tries int := 0; BEGIN LOOP BEGIN PERFORM set_config('lock_timeout', '300ms', true); LOCK TABLE orders IN ACCESS EXCLUSIVE MODE; ALTER TABLE orders ALTER COLUMN customer_id_new SET NOT NULL; ALTER TABLE orders DROP CONSTRAINT orders_customer_id_new_check; DROP TRIGGER orders_customer_id_sync ON orders; ALTER TABLE orders DROP COLUMN customer_id; ALTER TABLE orders RENAME COLUMN customer_id_new TO customer_id; EXIT; EXCEPTION WHEN lock_not_available THEN tries := tries + 1; IF tries >= 100 THEN RAISE; END IF; PERFORM pg_sleep(0.2); END; END LOOP; END $$;

steps.note: Drop the trigger function and refresh planner statistics for the new column.
steps.sql: DROP FUNCTION orders_customer_id_sync(); SET statement_timeout = 0; ANALYZE orders;

steps.note: Fail unless orders.customer_id is now bigint NOT NULL.
steps.sql: DO $$ BEGIN IF NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM information_schema.columns WHERE table_schema = 'public' AND table_name = 'orders' AND column_name = 'customer_id' AND data_type = 'bigint' AND is_nullable = 'NO') THEN RAISE EXCEPTION 'orders.customer_id is not bigint NOT NULL'; END IF; END $$;
